audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.


Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dello 0.3%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.4% e Hang Seng in rialzo del 2.5%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.


Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dello 0.26%, mentre il VIX è salito dello 0.75%, segnale di maggiore incertezza. L'oro ha guadagnato l'1.8%, raggiungendo quota $4555.6 l'oncia, mosso da timori sull'inflazione. Il petrolio è sceso dell'1.6%, a $93.46 al barile. Il rendimento del decennale USA è salito dello 0.49%, al 4.47%, e il BTP 10Y italiano è stabile al 3.73%.


In ambito geopolitico, l'inflazione nell'Eurozona è salita al 3.2% a maggio, spingendo la BCE a considerare un aumento dei tassi. Inoltre, la situazione in Medio Oriente sembra essersi schiarita, favorendo le borse europee.


Sul fronte macro, nessun dato rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sotto i settantamila dollari, precisamente a sessantanovemilatrecentocinquantatré dollari, con una flessione del 4,76% nella giornata. I flussi ETF hanno registrato una saída di 125,3 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle prese di profitto degli investitori dopo il recente rally.

Per quanto riguarda le altcoin, Ethereum scambia a mille novecentosettantadue dollari, con una lieve flessione dello 0,74%. Solana e BNB mostrano perdite più significative, rispettivamente del 2,47% e del 5,59%, a settantanove dollari e due centesimi e seicentosettantasei dollari e sedici centesimi.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 23, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 0.3%, Shanghai up 0.4%, and Hang Seng up 2.5%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the Western markets, during the previous session, the S&P 500 rose by 0.26%, while the VIX increased by 0.75%, a sign of greater uncertainty. Gold gained 1.8%, reaching $2,455.6 per ounce, driven by inflation fears. Oil fell 1.6%, to $93.46 per barrel. The 10-year US yield rose 0.49%, to 4.47%, and the Italian 10Y BTP is stable at 3.73%. In the geopolitical arena, Eurozone inflation rose to 3.2% in May, prompting the ECB to consider a rate hike. Furthermore, the situation in the Middle East seems to have cleared up, favoring European stock markets. On the macro front, no significant data out today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains below seventy thousand dollars, precisely at $69,353, with a decline of 4.76% on the day. ETF flows recorded an outflow of $125.3 million. This movement could be influenced by investors taking profits after the recent rally. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum trades at $1,972, with a slight decline of 0.74%. Solana and BNB show more significant losses, respectively of 2.47% and 5.59%, at $79.02 and $676.16 The Fear & Greed Index is at 23, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting caution among investors. No macro data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Deterring Russia Beneath the Waves: Securing NATO’s Critical Undersea Infrastructure
articles.snippet: What would happen if you woke up one morning and the internet was gone — not from a software glitch, but because someone had simply cut the wire?Threats to critical undersea infrastructure are rapidly escalating. In 2023, the Balticonnector pipeline and several Baltic data cables were damaged. A year later, four Red Sea cables were cut, disrupting a quarter of data traffic between Asia and Europe, with further incidents across the Baltic. In total, between January 2024 and July 2025, roughly 44 incidents of cable damage were recorded. Not all were deliberate, but Russia’s activity has grown brazen. articles.title: Monetary policy according to households: perceptions, reactions and channels
articles.snippet: by Francesco Grigoli, Damiano Sandri, Yuriy Gorodnichenko, Olivier Coibion This paper studies how households perceive the transmission of monetary policy and how these perceptions affect their decisions. Using a large-scale survey of over 25,000 U.S. households combined with randomized information treatments, we measure how households expect changes in the federal funds rate to affect economic conditions and their own behavior.

articles.title: Fences Not F-35s: Drone Attacks and the Illogic of Gulf Procurement

Under this scenario, consumer prices are set to rise to 4.8% while GDP growth would moderate to 6.3% from 6.7% previously expected, according to 360 ONE Capital, which…

articles.title: Europe’s Industrial Future Is Not Where Most People Think It Is
articles.snippet: For the past several years, Europe’s industrial debate has been dominated by a single word: decline. Factories are closing. Energy prices remain structurally higher than in competing regions. Germany’s industrial machine is under pressure. Steel, chemicals, fertilizers, and other energy-intensive sectors continue to struggle with the aftershocks of the gas crisis triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The conclusion often seems self-evident: Europe is deindustrializing. But reality is becoming far more complicated than the…
